_rule: External research says what the wider ecosystem does. It never overrides own-account analytics; disagreements are recorded.

findings.claim: Diwali 2026: Dhanteras Friday 6 November, Lakshmi Puja Sunday 8 November, five days 6-11 November; week 2026-10-26 sits 10-13 days before Diwali, the shopping and family-coordination window.
findings.source: Airalo festival calendar; Muhurat Choghadiya Diwali calendar (9 Oct 2026)

findings.claim: Saarva Festive Outlook Study 2026 (1,006 urban consumers, Sept 2026): 77% expect to spend more than a regular month; salaried consumers (82%) show stronger spend intent than business owners (65%); 15% are 'Budget Stretchers' who overshoot their set budget.
findings.source: Business Standard summarising the Saarva study (1 Oct 2026)

findings.claim: LocalCircles survey (Oct 2026): urban households plan an average of Rs 20,000 discretionary festive spend, down 6% year on year, and 83% of spending households will dip into savings; celebration with a tighter eye on the household budget.
findings.source: India Today summarising the LocalCircles survey (16 Oct 2026)

findings.claim: Relatives asking salary and marriage questions within minutes of meeting is a live viral theme: a founder's post about Indian relatives asking salary/marriage questions within 2 minutes trended on News18 (7 Oct 2026); an earlier Reddit story (HT, Oct 2025) called it an 'impromptu financial review' at a birthday party.

For Reels in 2026 the top ranking signals are watch time and sends per reach (DM shares); DM shares are the most heavily weighted signal for reel distribution; 30-90 second storytelling holds watch time best.

opportunities: Festive money pressure: shopping vs budget guilt (LocalCircles/Saarva both point to spend-with-caution), first salary giving decisions, and comparing what relatives can afford.
Festive-table interrogation: salary/marriage questions from relatives are a viral national theme right now; fits the confession register without copying any story.
Unseen home effort in the run-up to Diwali (cleaning, decorating, planning) going unnoticed; pairs with the family-coordination window.
